hook: Sigachi blast, one year on: families got about *₹41.5 lakh* of ₹1 crore
hook_b: Sigachi blast, one year on: families got about *₹41.5 lakh* of ₹1 crore
tldr: A year after the Sigachi Industries blast at Pashamylaram, widows, relatives and activists gathered to demand the full ₹1 crore compensation announced by the CM.

beats.what: Families say they received only about ₹41.5 lakh each; kin of casual and temporary workers got less, split among wives and mothers.
beats.why: CM Revanth Reddy announced ₹1 crore per family right after the blast, and the company told the stock exchanges it would pay ₹1 crore ex gratia.
beats.care: It tests what happens to compensation promises after industrial accidents in Telangana's pharma belt.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: TPJAC data: 19 families did not get the EDLI insurance payout, 13 did not get EPF dues and 11 did not get the Centre's compensation.

cards.q: Who should pay the remaining compensation?

qs: Who is legally liable for the remaining amount: the company or the state?
Why did casual and temporary workers' families get less?

facts.t: The company reportedly told the High Court its liability was discharged at *₹42 lakh* per family.
*19 families* did not receive the EDLI insurance payout, per TPJAC data.

viz.verdict: Families say they got well under half of what was announced
Dozens of families still waiting on insurance and PF dues

learn.t: EDLI = Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance, a life cover linked to a worker's PF account

watch: Whether the state pays the balance, and what the High Court says in the PIL on compensation.

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.title: CM's promise of ₹1 crore a mirage for Sigachi blast victims' kin in Telangana

fact: Sigachi blast families say they got about *₹41.5 lakh*, not the ₹1 crore promised
twist: The company reportedly told the High Court its liability ended at ₹42 lakh per family, with the rest to be paid by the government.
